headline: High: Windsurf’s shared filesystem and broad egress can leak dbt-core workspace data and create unsafe cross-agent interactions by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf reads workspace files, uses MCP servers, and shares state via local filesystem; dbt-core can call a data warehouse and handle warehouse data. That creates a plausible path where content from dbt artifacts or files is treated as instructions by Windsurf. No direct prompt-parser evidence exists, so uncertainty stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF dbt-core writes attacker-controlled SQL or model text into shared workspace files
IF Windsurf ingests those files or MCP outputs as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of workspace-generated text into agent prompts
Separate dbt artifacts from Windsurf-readable folders
Add a manual review step before Windsurf acts on file content
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tagging on shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress; Windsurf reads workspace files, uses broad egress, and handles model-provider keys. If warehouse outputs or open files enter Windsurf’s context, they can be transmitted off-box through its model proxy or MCP path. The pair therefore has a realistic exfiltration pathway in default use.
conditions: IF dbt-core materializes warehouse rows into workspace files
IF Windsurf sends those files or prompts to its model proxy or MCP servers
mitigations: Restrict Windsurf to non-sensitive workspaces
Block outbound access from the workspace host except approved endpoints
Remove secrets and warehouse extracts from shared folders
Turn off auto-upload of file context where possible
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on workspace-to-model traffic

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can operate on warehouse data while Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and use a per-window session with shared local filesystem state. That overlap makes concurrent edits to the same repo or artifacts likely to race and corrupt state, especially because no locking mechanism is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace directory
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while dbt-core is generating or updating artifacts
mitigations: Run the agents in separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes repo state
Use git branches per agent
Avoid auto-execute for filesystem-mutating commands
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can generate warehouse-derived outputs that Windsurf may read from workspace files and then act on with shell, git, or subprocess tools. That makes A’s outputs a plausible upstream input to B’s actions, but Windsurf’s approval-per-command default provides some verification, so this is not high by default.
conditions: IF Windsurf treats dbt-generated files or logs as authoritative
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled for commands derived from dbt output
mitigations: Require human review of dbt outputs before actioning them
Disable auto-execute for commands sourced from generated files
Keep dbt artifacts and action scripts in separate directories
Add checksum or schema validation before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core is documented as touching data warehouse data, while Windsurf handles open files and model-provider keys with broad network egress. If regulated warehouse data or secrets are placed into Windsurf’s workspace, the pair can create a retention and residency mismatch. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR status, so this is a compliance-risk inference rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied from the warehouse into Windsurf-opened files
IF Windsurf’s model proxy or logs retain that data longer than the warehouse policy allows
mitigations: Keep regulated datasets out of the IDE workspace
Review Windsurf retention and logging settings
Use synthetic or masked data for development
Separate secrets from files opened in Windsurf
requires-engineering: document and enforce a data-handling policy
